headline: Private Credit Is Scary. Get Those High Yields Without the Risk.
summary: For investors put off by private credit, there are high-yielding alternatives without the baggage.  Broadly syndicated loans, generally originated by banks, are similar to private-credit loans because both go to speculative-grade companies and typically carry floating rates tied to the Secured Overnight Financing Rate, or SOFR, the short-term yield benchmark now around 3.7%.

headline: Private credit risks more deep-seated than headlines suggest: Investor
summary: Robert Dafforn, Chief Investment Officer at Polus Capital Management, tells CNBC’s Ritika Gupta that significant risks in private credit have been building for years, well before the sector came under broader scrutiny. He warns that continued outflows and investor redemptions could ultimately cause capital to dry up across the market.

headline: Still Looking for the Next Warren Buffett? We Found ‘Him.’
summary: As Warren Buffett exits the stage, it’s reasonable to ask: Who will become the next ultimate sage of American business?  First, we’re coming up on  Berkshire Hathaway’s  annual meeting on Saturday, May 2, where for the first time in 60 years, Buffett, 95—arguably the leading voice of American business for decades—won’t be on stage leading the flock.  Because Buffett’s skill set is so multidimensional, filling his shoes is almost like replacing a combination of Michael Jordan, Tiger Woods, and Wayne Gretzky.
